text:
Ben Kindel is 19, already in his second NHL season, and playing real minutes for a Penguins team that keeps losing. He has 9 points in 18 games at about 17 and a half minutes a night, after a short stint out in late October, and he scored the power-play goal in the shootout win in San Jose on Nov. 11.

The points undersell him. With Kindel on the ice, Pittsburgh has scored 12.2 fewer goals than its chances deserved, the kind of gap that usually swings back. His own finishing is only a goal behind his expected goals (the quality of his chances), so this is mostly his linemates and goalies on the wrong side of the dice.

The worry is the other end: the Penguins get under half of the expected goals at five on five with him out there. Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking had him carrying the puck in on 56% of his entries last season, and that's the habit to watch. Our range for his season lands around 43 points.
headline: Kindel's second year is better than it looks
